findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the re-export-completeness AC command executable as written: define `refs()` as a shell function (e.g. `refs() { { grep ...; grep ...; } | sort -u; }`) run under bash, or replace process substitution with intermediate temp files, so `comm -23` receives real inputs.
evidence: "with `refs` defined as `{ grep -rhoE ... }` ... the command `comm -23 <(refs) <(printf '%s\n' ...)` produces NO output"
Process substitution `<(...)` is a bash/zsh feature not present in POSIX sh/dash; a brace group named in prose is not an executable command name.
findings.finding: The re-export-completeness proving command in AC line 4 uses `comm -23 <(refs) <(printf ...)`, but `refs` is only described as 'defined as `{ ...; }`' — a brace group, not a shell function or alias. As literally written, `<(refs)` invokes a command named `refs`, which does not exist, so the command errors ('refs: command not found') rather than proving the invariant; additionally process substitution `<(...)` is bash-only and silently unavailable under dash/sh, so an operator could believe the check ran when it did not.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, final bullet (comm-based re-export completeness check)
findings.suggested_fix: Define `refs() { { grep -rhoE 'event_append\.(_[A-Za-z_]+|subprocess)' tests/ --include=*.py | sed 's/^event_append\.//'; grep -rhoE '(set|get)attr\(event_append, "[^"]+"' tests/ --include=*.py | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]+)"/\1/'; } | sort -u; }` and run the `comm` line under `bash -c`.
